title: What are all the factors of these five numbers?
description: Five numbers are broken into primes, and groups of the primes are multiplied to list every factor, with one added. The lists for ninety and one hundred and five come first, then the longer lists for three hundred and sixty and eight hundred and forty. A check pairs up the factors of ninety and counts the last two lists.
teaching_notes: One idea: every factor of a number is a group of its primes multiplied together, and one is a factor too. Watch for students who list only the prime factors or who miss a factor in the long lists.

video_script.why: The child must list every factor of larger numbers without missing any, using the primes as the book does.
video_script.substitution: Write the primes of the number, multiply groups of the primes to get the factors, and add the factor one.
video_script.anchor: The five numbers written in a row, each with its primes beneath it.

final_answer.spoken: ninety has twelve factors, one hundred and five has eight, one hundred and thirty two has twelve, three hundred and sixty has twenty four, and eight hundred and forty has thirty two

never_show: a list of factors that holds only the primes
maths_rules: Slip: 6 x 15 = 90, so 6 and 15 are factors of 90 although they are not prime.
video_script.design: One idea: groups of the primes, multiplied, give every factor, and one is added. Assumes the child can break a number into primes. The five numbers stay on the board all video.
